text: Contesting the view that the 2008 crisis was an American problem inflicted on foreign victims, the authors argue that non U.S. institutions such as German banks were willing participants in the risk taking, even where they did not fully understand the risks they assumed.
citation: Painter and Kaal, Initial Reflections on an Evolving Standard Constraints on Risk Taking by Directors and Officers in (2010). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1558614

isBasedOn.name: Initial Reflections on an Evolving Standard Constraints on Risk Taking by Directors and Officers in

abstract: The experience of German banks with CDOs, however, revealed that some of the non- U.S. victims were willing participants in the risk, even if they did not always fully understand the risks.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: applies to European banks that bought or sponsored U.S. structured credit products
